title: Trying to Improve My Geography Game with More Real-World Data
beats: Recap of last video's flying game; problem: GPU timeout on other machines
Bisect by lowering all resolutions then restoring one by one; culprit is country-index compute shader; bake it to an image instead of optimizing
Colour map too small; rescale 8 tiles to 8k, accept 256MB; swap to a less snowy month
Detour to the Eye of the Sahara; 3 arc-second data is about 90 m per pixel; render a flat 540 km2 area, 8x exaggeration, fly there
Return to the 8 tiles: lat/long wrap pinches at poles, so match 96 cube-sphere pieces to correct tile via centre point inverse mapping
Admits his words may not make sense, shows an animation of what the code does; shader remaps texture coordinates
Camera jitter fixed by built-in LookAt; he does not understand the cause
City lights painted on terrain stretch on slopes; switch to individual points chosen by random sampling and keeping the brightest
Light shader with time-of-day value; tweak size, colour; harsh on/off line fixed with per-light random offset
Increase time variation, see the line break up; add bloom (brightest parts, blur, add back)
Mesh has 8.6M vertices; flat areas need fewer than mountains; goal is fewer while keeping perceived detail
Three failed attempts shown quickly (nonsense output), skip frustrating hours
Error = height minus average of 4 neighbours; keep point if above threshold; grid floor for flat curved areas
Raise threshold in steps: ocean loses points first, then more; trade off detail vs performance
Triangulation delegated to Triangle library; 9M to 1M vertices; cleverer LOD exists but later
Silhouette matters, normal map covers lighting detail; cache result to file
Wind data: unfamiliar format converted to JSON; u and v components as velocity along axes
Visualise speed, then direction as red/green, then moving particles on the vector field
Cyclones rotate counterclockwise in the north, opposite in south, used as sanity check
Not sure how to use wind in game; leave experiment
Moon: colour and height map, normal map, sphere, then circular orbit with locked rotation
Predict libration: tilt makes up/down rocking, ellipse should add side-to-side and size change
Compare Newton n-body simulation vs analytic orbit; choose periapsis and apoapsis to define ellipse
Kepler equal-area fact turned into equation relating circular position to elliptical angle E
No exact solution, so rearrange to zero-finding and guess with Newton's method; points to another video
calculate point on orbit; satellite speeds near planet, slows far; apply to moon with 360k-405k km
White line to Earth, red line facing direction shows lag and lead in rotation
Earth orbit around sun and tilt: low sun in winter, high in summer
Draw sun trail by day: analemma figure 8; make orbit circular to balance lobes; zero tilt gives a single point
Stars from a catalogue filtered by apparent magnitude; check Sirius and the north star
Atmosphere: sky rendered tiny and upscaled; terrain via 3D texture slices by depth, two textures for scattering and transmittance
Show scattering alone, transmittance alone, terrain colour alone, then combined
Fly through the result, caveats on Earth shadow, ocean wave noise, lakes, still no gameplay

metrics.key_term: error-threshold mesh simplification / Kepler orbit equation via Newton's method
metrics.misconception: partial: assumed distribution of cheap optimization of compute shader (1:00) and that evenly distributed points are needed everywhere (12:27)
metrics.brute_force: yes 13:04: three failed mesh-reduction attempts shown; also random sampling of candidate light positions (9:12)
metrics.examples: many tweaks; the orbit section grows moon circle -> ellipse -> sun/earth -> analemma; the mesh section grows threshold 0 -> small -> larger
metrics.ending: Casual wrap and release plans; no recap of lessons

principles.2: partly: periapsis, apoapsis, u-component introduced only when used (23:48, 17:26); Kepler's equation shown late and briefly
principles.4: partly: no analogy but physical picture first (what we see from Earth, equal-area wedge at 24:21)
principles.5: partly: fly the plane to the Eye of the Sahara; draw lines on the moon to see its facing (26:34)
principles.6: confirmed: error threshold mesh (14:03) and randomised sampling for lights (9:12) are the simple approach; failures at 13:04 show the dumb path first
principles.7: partly: threshold slider sweep (14:52) and analemma toggles (28:16) let learner see the cause, but explanation comes straight from the presenter
principles.8: not-observed: pace set by project beats; idea rate slows in failures (13:22-14:03 skipped) and speeds through code he labels uninteresting
principles.9: confirmed: compute shader plus instancing pattern repeated for lights (9:12), wind particles (18:50), stars (29:13); tweak-and-view loop repeats
principles.10: confirmed: circular orbit to ellipse to full sun/earth orbit and analemma; threshold small to larger
principles.11: partly: orbit pieces ordered (shape, then time, then equation); the whole video is a chronological list
principles.12: confirmed: Earth Explorer, NWS wind data, Kepler, Newton's method video, Triangle library, paper on atmosphere, bloom tutorial
principles.13: partly: tools chosen with reasons (why not texture, why points); some steps delegated with 'I do not understand' (8:20)

new_moves.name: ablation-by-toggle
new_moves.what: Remove one cause at a time in the simulation to attribute each visual feature to its cause
new_moves.evidence: 28:16-28:34 circular orbit balances lobes, zero tilt collapses analemma

new_moves.name: visual-layer-peeling
new_moves.what: Show each component alone then combined so the learner sees what each contributes
new_moves.evidence: 32:08-32:24 scattering, transmittance, terrain colour, then all together

new_moves.name: external-sanity-check
new_moves.what: Verify a build with a known real-world fact
new_moves.evidence: 19:56 cyclone direction by hemisphere; 29:46 north star; 29:13 Sirius

new_moves.name: skip-the-grind-edit
new_moves.what: Compresses failed attempts into a few seconds and says hours were skipped

theory: The video teaches design decisions by letting a single measurable knob (error threshold, time variation, tilt) be turned on screen so the cause of each visual change is seen directly. Honest scope limits and sanity checks against reality make a loosely organised devlog trustworthy, but the explanation of why Kepler plus Newton works is thin compared with what the visuals do.
velocity: Scene builder: expose one parameter slider per concept and let ghost hands sweep it while the voice names the effect
Orchestrator: after a build, add an external sanity-check beat (known fact the result must match)
Evals: check that every new term appears after the scene using it, e.g. periapsis at 23:48
Voice: use 'I do not understand why, but...' sparingly and label it, never hide it
Scene builder: layer-peeling mode that toggles components on and off in sequence
quote: skip over a few frustrating hours
